## phenix experiment capture

Experiment capture management

### Synopsis

```text
Experiment capture management

  An experiment capture records the traffic of all the VLANs, or of the given
  VLANs, of a running experiment on all its hosts into one file in the
  experiment's files directory. It needs a minimega build that has the
  experiment capture commands; phenix does not check the minimega version.
```

```text
phenix experiment capture [flags]
```

### Options

```text
  -h, --help   help for capture
```

### SEE ALSO

* [phenix experiment](experiment.md) - Experiment management
* [phenix experiment capture list](experiment.md#phenix-experiment-capture-list) - List the experiment captures of an experiment
* [phenix experiment capture start](experiment.md#phenix-experiment-capture-start) - Start an experiment capture
* [phenix experiment capture stop](experiment.md#phenix-experiment-capture-stop) - Stop an experiment capture

## phenix experiment capture start

Start an experiment capture

### Synopsis

```text
Start an experiment capture

  Starts one packet capture of the running experiment's traffic, on every
  VLAN or on the VLANs that --vlan gives, and prints its ID, its file and the
  Open vSwitch mirror budget warnings. phenix refuses the start when a host
  and bridge that the capture needs has 32 mirrors.
```

```text
phenix experiment capture start <experiment name> [flags]
```

### Examples

```text
phenix experiment capture start exp1
phenix experiment capture start exp1 --vlan EXP_1 --vlan EXP_2 --filter "tcp port 502" --format pcap
```

### Options

```text
      --filter string      BPF filter of the frames to capture
      --format string      capture file format, pcapng or pcap (default "pcapng")
  -h, --help               help for start
      --name string        file name in the experiment's files directory (default <exp>[-<vlan>]-<time>)
      --snaplen int        most bytes of each frame to keep, from 14 to 65535 (0 keeps 1600)
      --vlan stringArray   VLAN alias to capture (repeat for more; all VLANs when not given)
```

### SEE ALSO

* [phenix experiment capture](experiment.md#phenix-experiment-capture) - Experiment capture management

## phenix experiment create

Create an experiment

### Synopsis

```text
Create an experiment

  Used to create an experiment from existing configurations; can be a
  topology, or topology and scenario, or paths to topology/scenario
  configuration files (YAML or JSON). (Optional are the arguments for
  scenario or base directory.)
```

```text

```

### Examples


## phenix experiment delete

Delete an experiment

### Synopsis

```text
Delete an experiment

  Used to delete an existing experiment; experiment must be stopped.
  Using 'all' instead of a specific experiment name will include all
  stopped experiments. Use the -f/--force flag to automatically stop
  a running experiment before deleting it.

  When phenix cannot stop or delete an experiment, it continues with the
  other experiments. Then it exits with an error that names each failure.

  With --dry-run, phenix shows the experiments that it would stop and
  delete, and changes nothing.
```

```text
phenix experiment delete <experiment name> [flags]
```

### Options

```text
      --dry-run   Show what the command would change, and change nothing
  -f, --force     Stop a running experiment before deleting it
  -h, --help      help for delete
```

### SEE ALSO

* [phenix experiment](experiment.md) - Experiment management

## phenix experiment files archive

Write experiment files to a local zip archive

### Synopsis

```text
Write experiment files to a local zip archive

  Archives the files as the Files tab's archive does, with the same limits:
  at most 500 files and 2 GiB in total. A file that phenix cannot add is
  left out, and the MISSING.txt entry of the archive names it with the
  reason; the command then fails after it writes the archive.
```

```text
phenix experiment files archive <experiment name> <file>... --output-file <zip file> [flags]
```

### Examples

```text
phenix experiment files archive exp1 web_eth0.pcap db_eth0.pcap -O captures.zip
```

### Options

```text
  -h, --help                 help for archive
  -O, --output-file string   write the zip archive to this path (required)
```

## phenix experiment files delete

Delete experiment files from every node

### Synopsis

```text
Delete experiment files from every node

  Deletes each file from the head node and from every mesh node that has it.
  Refuses a file that is not in the list of the experiment's files, and a
  packet capture that minimega still writes. The command deletes the files it
  can, names each file it does not delete with the reason, and then fails.

  With --dry-run, phenix checks each file as for a delete, shows the files
  that it would delete, and deletes nothing.
```

```text
phenix experiment files delete <experiment name> <file>... [flags]
```

### Options

```text
      --dry-run   Show what the command would change, and change nothing
  -h, --help      help for delete
```

* [phenix experiment files](experiment.md#phenix-experiment-files) - Experiment file management

## phenix experiment files get

Write an experiment file to stdout or to a local file

### Synopsis

```text
Write an experiment file to stdout or to a local file

  Refuses a packet capture that minimega still writes: stop the capture
  first. With --output-file, phenix writes the file next to the given path
  first, and replaces the given path only when the copy is complete.
  Without --output-file, phenix does not write a binary file, such as a
  packet capture, to a terminal.
```

```text
phenix experiment files get <experiment name> <file> [flags]
```

### Examples

```text
# Copy a capture from a sub folder to the current folder
phenix experiment files get exp1 captures/web_eth0.pcap -O web_eth0.pcap
```

### Options

```text
  -h, --help                 help for get
  -O, --output-file string   write the file to this path instead of stdout
```

* [phenix experiment files](experiment.md#phenix-experiment-files) - Experiment file management

## phenix experiment reconfigure

Reconfigure an experiment

### Synopsis

```text
Reconfigure an experiment

  Used to rerun the 'configure' stage of all the apps (both default and user)
  for the given experiment (as long as it's not running). Using 'all' instead
  of a specific experiment name will reconfigure all non-running
  experiments.

  This differs from 'phenix experiment trigger <experiment name> configure'
  in that it re-runs config validation and any registered config hooks, and
  always applies to all apps. Use this after editing an experiment's stored
  topology, scenario, or deployment settings. Use 'trigger configure' to
  manually re-run a specific app's (or apps') configure hook on demand for
  debugging; note it does not validate the config, run config hooks, or
  guard against running experiments the way 'reconfigure' does.
```

```text
phenix experiment reconfigure <experiment name> [flags]
```

### Options

```text
  -h, --help   help for reconfigure
```

### SEE ALSO

* [phenix experiment](experiment.md) - Experiment management

## phenix experiment restart

Restart an experiment

### Synopsis

```text
Restart an experiment

  Used to restart a running experiment, using 'all' instead of a specific
  experiment name will include all running experiments; dry-run will do
  everything but call out to minimega.

  Before phenix stops the experiment, it checks the disk images and CD-ROM
  images of the VMs as 'phenix experiment start' does. A missing file
  refuses the restart, and the experiment continues to run. When the
  scenario has a user app, the app can change the disks, so this check
  only shows warnings, and the check before the start can still refuse it.

  The stop of the experiment takes the flags of 'phenix experiment stop'
  (--force and --keep-injection-snapshots), and its start takes the flags
  of 'phenix experiment start'. With --treat-mm-errors-as-warnings, the
  check before the stop shows the problems as warnings.

  NOTE: passing the --honor-run-periodically flag will prevent the CLI from
  returning. If Ctrl+c is pressed, the experiment will continue to run but
  the running stage will no longer continue to be triggered for any apps
  configured (via the scenario) to have their running stage triggered
  periodically.
```

```text
phenix experiment restart <experiment name> [flags]
```

### Options

```text
      --dry-run                       Do everything but actually call out to minimega
  -f, --force                         Mark the experiment stopped even if minimega cannot kill its VMs
  -h, --help                          help for restart
      --honor-run-periodically        Periodically trigger running stage in apps if configured in scenario
  -K, --keep-injection-snapshots      Keep VM injection snapshots after stopping
      --treat-mm-errors-as-warnings   Treat errors from minimega as warnings instead of failing
      --vlan-max int                  VLAN pool maximum for this start (1-4094; 0 keeps the maximum of the experiment)
      --vlan-min int                  VLAN pool minimum for this start (1-4094; 0 keeps the minimum of the experiment)
```

### SEE ALSO

* [phenix experiment](experiment.md) - Experiment management

## phenix experiment scorch

Start a Scorch run for experiment

### Synopsis

```text
Start a Scorch run for an experiment

  Used to start the Scorch run that --run selects (0 when not given) for the
  given experiment, and to wait until it ends. The command prints the
  progress of the run, and exits with an error when the run fails.

  When phenix ui is running, the server executes the run, so the web UI
  shows it and can cancel it. Ctrl+C cancels the run on the server. When
  phenix ui is not running, this command executes the run in its own
  process. The web UI does not show that run.

  The --status, --cancel, --cleanup and --clear flags need phenix ui. Each
  acts on the run that --run selects, and only one can be given:

    --status   shows the status of each stage and component of the run
    --cancel   cancels the run on the server
    --cleanup  runs only the cleanup stage of the run, and waits for it
    --clear    clears the status of a run that is not executing

  -o/--output sets the output format of --status. With --cancel or --clear,
  --dry-run checks that the server has the run, shows what phenix would
  request, and requests nothing.
```

```text
phenix experiment scorch <experiment name> [flags]
```

### Examples

```text
# Run Scorch run 1 and wait until it ends
phenix experiment scorch exp1 --run 1

# Show the status of Scorch run 1
phenix experiment scorch exp1 --run 1 --status

# Cancel Scorch run 1 on the server
phenix experiment scorch exp1 --run 1 --cancel

# The status of Scorch run 1 as JSON
phenix experiment scorch exp1 --run 1 --status -o json
```

### Options

```text
      --cancel          Cancel the run on the server (needs phenix ui)
      --cleanup         Run only the cleanup stage of the run (needs phenix ui)
      --clear           Clear the status of the run (needs phenix ui)
      --dry-run         Show what the command would change, and change nothing
  -h, --help            help for scorch
  -o, --output string   Output format (text, json, yaml) (default "text")
  -r, --run int         ID of the Scorch run to act on (defaults to 0)
      --status          Show the status of the run (needs phenix ui)
```

### SEE ALSO

* [phenix experiment](experiment.md) - Experiment management

## phenix experiment soh

Show the state of health of experiments

### Synopsis

```text
Show the state of health of experiments

  Without an experiment, shows a summary of each experiment on one row, as
  the State of Health page does: the state of the soh app, the running VMs,
  and the checks that passed in its latest run. With an experiment, shows
  each of its VMs with its status and failing checks, then the failing
  checks of the latest run. --status shows only the VMs with that status.
```

```text

```

### Examples

```text
# The VMs of exp1 that do not run
phenix experiment soh exp1 --status notrunning

# The summary of each experiment as JSON
phenix experiment soh -o json
```

### Options

```text
  -h, --help            help for soh
  -o, --output string   Output format (table, json, yaml) (default "table")
      --status string   only the VMs with this status (running, notrunning, notboot, notdeploy, external)
```

### SEE ALSO

* [phenix experiment](experiment.md) - Experiment management

## phenix experiment start

Start an experiment

### Synopsis

```text
Start an experiment

  Used to start a stopped experiment, using 'all' instead of a specific
  experiment name will include all stopped experiments; dry-run will do
  everything but call out to minimega.

  Before minimega launches a VM, phenix checks that each disk image and
  CD-ROM image of the VMs exists, and that the backing chain of each disk
  image is complete. A missing file refuses the start and lists each VM,
  disk and missing file. With --dry-run or --treat-mm-errors-as-warnings,
  phenix shows the problems as warnings. The experiment.disk-check setting
  changes this for every start: warn shows the problems as warnings, and
  off skips the check.

  NOTE: passing the --honor-run-periodically flag will prevent the CLI from
  returning. If Ctrl+c is pressed, the experiment will continue to run but
  the running stage will no longer continue to be triggered for any apps
  configured (via the scenario) to have their running stage triggered
  periodically.
```

```text
phenix experiment start <experiment name> [flags]
```

### Options

```text
      --dry-run                       Do everything but actually call out to minimega
  -h, --help                          help for start
      --honor-run-periodically        Periodically trigger running stage in apps if configured in scenario
      --treat-mm-errors-as-warnings   Treat errors from minimega as warnings instead of failing
      --vlan-max int                  VLAN pool maximum for this start (1-4094; 0 keeps the maximum of the experiment)
      --vlan-min int                  VLAN pool minimum for this start (1-4094; 0 keeps the minimum of the experiment)
```

### SEE ALSO

* [phenix experiment](experiment.md) - Experiment management

## phenix experiment stop

Stop an experiment

### Synopsis

```text
Stop an experiment

  Used to stop a running experiment, using 'all' instead of a specific
  experiment name will include all running experiments. An experiment whose
  VMs minimega cannot kill stays running; --force marks it stopped anyway.
```

```text
phenix experiment stop <experiment name> [flags]
```

### Options

```text
  -f, --force                      Mark the experiment stopped even if minimega cannot kill its VMs
  -h, --help                       help for stop
  -K, --keep-injection-snapshots   Keep VM injection snapshots after stopping
```

### SEE ALSO

* [phenix experiment](experiment.md) - Experiment management

## phenix experiment trigger

Trigger lifecycle stage for app(s) in experiment

### Synopsis

```text
Trigger an app lifecycle stage in an experiment

  Used to manually trigger the "configure", "pre-start", "post-start", "running",
  or "cleanup" stage of an app (or apps) for the given experiment on demand.
  Using 'all' instead of a specific experiment name triggers the stage for the
  given app(s) in all experiments. Providing no apps triggers the stage for all
  apps in the experiment(s). The "running" stage is skipped for stopped
  experiments.

  Triggering the "configure" stage is not the same as
  'phenix experiment reconfigure': this command does not validate the
  experiment config, run config hooks, or guard against running
  experiments. Use 'phenix experiment reconfigure' after
  editing an experiment's stored topology, scenario, or deployment settings.

  This command runs the stage in its own process. Ctrl+C stops a trigger
  that this command runs. --cancel stops the triggers that phenix ui runs,
  which the web UI or the REST API started: give no lifecycle with it, and
  give app names to stop only those apps. Without app names, --cancel also
  ends the scheduled runs of the running stage that phenix ui runs after a
  start (the experiments.periodic job). --cancel needs phenix ui. With
  --cancel --dry-run, phenix shows the cancels that it would request, and
  requests none.

  The old argument order, <lifecycle> <experiment name> [<app name> ...],
  is deprecated. It still works, with a warning, when no experiment has the
  lifecycle as its name.

  Valid lifecycles and shorthands: configure (config), pre-start (pre), post-start (post), running (run), cleanup (clean).
```

```text
phenix experiment trigger <experiment name> <lifecycle> [<app name> ...] [flags]
```

### Examples

```text
# Run the configure stage of every app of exp1
phenix experiment trigger exp1 configure

# Run the running stage of the soh app in every experiment
phenix experiment trigger all running soh

# Stop the soh trigger that phenix ui runs for exp1
phenix experiment trigger exp1 --cancel soh
```

### Options

```text
      --cancel    Stop the triggers that phenix ui runs for the experiment (needs phenix ui)
      --dry-run   Show what the command would change, and change nothing
  -h, --help      help for trigger
```

### SEE ALSO

* [phenix experiment](experiment.md) - Experiment management
